newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-GRISSOM HOMER IN 10TH LIFTS INDIANS PAST YANKEES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-GRISSOM HOMER IN 10TH LIFTS INDIANS PAST YANKEES.

text.p: Marquis Grissom homered off relief ace Mariano Rivera with one out in the top of the 10th inning to beat the New York Yankees 3-2 Monday and extend the Cleveland Indians' winning streak to four games.

Grissom belted an 0-2 pitch from the major league saves leader to the opposite field, over the fence in right-centre field. It was his fourth homer of the season and the fourth surrendered by Rivera (2-3).

"You just want to get a hit in that situation," Grissom said. "When a guy's throwing that hard, you've got to just try and hit the ball hard. You can't worry about where you're going to hit it. I knew I hit it pretty good. When it went over the fence it was a pretty good feeling."
"He put good wood on the ball," Rivera said. "It was a fastball and he just hit it out."

On Sunday, Grissom saw his 11-game hitting streak end as he was the only Indians starter without a hit in a 12-run explosion. He bounced back with three hits, a pair of runs scored and a diving catch in centre field.
Mike Jackson (2-1), the fourth Cleveland pitcher, struck out two in two perfect innings to get the win.
"We had it snatched away from us," Yankees manager Joe Torre said. "The only time we were behind in the game was when we lost. It's frustrating."
Yankee starter David Wells surrendered two runs and nine hits in 7 1/3 innings.
Matt Williams hit a solo homer for Cleveland.

In Boston, Wil Cordero -- under a cloud over alleged wife-beating -- had three hits, including a two-run homer, and every Red Sox starter had at least two hits and one RBI in an 18-4 rout of the Detroit Tigers, snapping a three-game losing streak.

Cordero went 3-for-5 with three RBI and two runs scored. He had been hitless in 10 at-bats since returning to the lineup on Thursday. He was charged with assaulting his wife on June 11 and the team tried to trade him. He did not speak to the media after the game.
John Valentin collected three hits and two RBI and Mike Stanley, Darren Bragg and Jeff Frye each had two hits and two RBI for Boston, which banged out a season-high 21 hits.
Jeff Suppan (3-0) was the beneficiary of the runs. Kevin Jarvis (0-1), making his first start of the season for the Tigers after three relief appearances, took the loss.

In Baltimore, pinch-hitter Tony Tarasco ignited a six-run seventh inning with a two-run single and Brady Anderson and Geronimo Berroa had two RBI each as the Orioles snapped a season-high six-game losing streak with a 9-5 victory over the Toronto Blue Jays.
Tarasco is 3-for-4 with two walks and four RBI as a pinch-hitter this year.

In Kansas City, Scott Cooper's one-out single in the bottom of the 14th scored Mike Macfarlane with the winning run as the Royals edged the Milwaukee Brewers 2-1, ending a franchise-record 12-game losing streak.

The win also was the first under manager Tony Muser, who replaced Bob Boone at the All-Star break after the Royals lost their last eight games before the Mid-Summer Classic. Muser won for the first time in five games as Royals manager.

In Minnesota, Ron Coomer's RBI double with one out in the sixth snapped a tie and Frank Rodriguez (2-3) won for the first time in nearly three months as the Twins ended the Chicago White Sox' seven-game winning streak, 5-3.
Rodriguez allowed one hit in two scoreless innings.
Doug Drabek (6-7) took the loss.
Albert Belle and Frank Thomas each had two hits for Chicago.

In Anaheim, Dave Hollins' one-out, two-run, 0-2 single in the bottom of the ninth scored Gary DiSarcina and Tony Phillips to rally the Angels past the Texas Rangers, 6-5, and extend their winning streak to seven games.
Texas closer John Wetteland (4-2), who came on to start the eighth, took the loss. Kevin Gross (2-1) earned the victory, pitching a scoreless ninth.
Juan Gonzalez, Bill Ripken, Dean Palmer and Warren Newson homered for Texas.
In Oakland, Jay Buhner launched a mammoth two-run homer in the first as the Seattle Mariners beat the Athletics 6-2.

Bob Wolcott (5-4) allowed two runs over seven strong innings. He extended his personal winning streak to three games by surrendering eight hits, walking none and striking out four. He surrendered a pair of solo homers to Matt Stairs.
Buhner's 24th homer of the season was a 436-foot (133-metres) blast deep into the left-field bleachers to give the Mariners a quick 3-0 lead against Steve Wojciechowski (0-1).
